newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania launch regional passport.
newsitem.headline: Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania launch regional passport.

text.p: The presidents of Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania launched a regional passport on Tuesday and endorsed a strategy to promote regional cooperation.
Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi, as chairman of the summit in the Tanzanian town Arusha, said he wished East African states had not broken up the East African Community 20 years ago.
"Regional economic blocs provide larger markets than individual countries. As a bloc, countries are better placed to bargain for better terms of trade with others," he said.
"This is the challenge facing us in this region and indeed the entire sub-Saharan Africa, to unite and fortify themselves into a solid regional trading block," he added.

"If you are a Tanzanian or a Kenyan or a Ugandan be patriotic to your country first and then to East Africa so as to bring about required development because nobody will ever do this for us, he said."
"Whatever successes we have attained, and whatever plans we have for the future, they all depend on our ability as governments to maintain peace, security and trust in our region," he said.

The Community collapsed in 1977, with former Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere saying his Kenyan counterpart Jomo Kenyatta headed a "man-eat-man society" while Kenyatta portrayed Kenya as better than Tanzania's "man-eat-nothing" society.
The three countries have renewed efforts in recent years to promote economic cooperation for the region's estimated 70 million people.
Kenya's biggest African trading parners remain Uganda and Tanzania although these countries have complained of a huge trade imbalance in favour of their neighbour.

In a communique at the end of their meeting, the presidents noted they had agreed in recent months on convertibility of currencies, pre- and post-budget consultations by finance officials, and presentation of budgets on the same day.
